chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to them from Safwan ibn Khalid from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muhajir from Al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Which is closer: the son of a paternal uncle (on both father and mother's side) or the paternal uncle (on father's side)?"

I said - Abu Ishaq al-Sabii narrated to me - from Al-Harith al-A'war from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that he used to say: "The specific maternal uncles are closer than the paternal uncles (of the father only)."

He (Al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah) said: So he sat up straight and then said: "You brought it from a clear source. Indeed, 'Abdullah (the father of the Prophet) was the brother of Abu Talib on both his father and mother."

key_terms.بَنِي الْأُمِّ: Maternal uncles (sons of the mother's sisters/brothers)
key_terms.بَنِي الْعَلَّاتِ: Paternal uncles (specifically of the father, not full)

ai.seo_question: Who is closer in inheritance: the paternal uncle or the maternal uncle according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the hierarchy of inheritance closeness (qurb) by distinguishing between full paternal uncles and those related through the father only, ultimately prioritizing maternal uncles based on the precedent of Imam Ali. The Imam validates this ruling by citing the Prophet’s lineage, noting that Abdullah (the Prophet’s father) and Abu Talib were full brothers, thereby establishing the principle that shared parentage confers greater closeness. This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes among collateral relatives, emphasizing that kinship through both parents outweighs that through a single parent.
